status: held-out protocol frozen before any v0.7 model call
task_suite: PrefixSum v0.1, adapted from Silo-Bench II-11
task_split: all generated cases held out; no prompt tuning on these seeds
runtime: llama.cpp b11202, commit fcb3074f2, Windows x64 CUDA 12.4
interaction_scaffold: Coordination rules: agent IDs are zero-based. Agent 0 sends the needed information to Agent 1; Agent 1 receives it and computes its segment. Do not target yourself. Each agent must submit a JSON list of integers containing only the global prefix sums for its own segment, in order. Agent 0 computes its local cumulative sums. Agent 1 adds Agent 0's segment total to every local cumulative sum; if the received message contains a full segment, sum it first. Submit the list with submit_result as soon as it is correct. Do not repeat messages or poll after receiving the needed information.

conditions.concise_nl: When sending a message, communicate only the sum of all values in your local segment as one short English sentence exactly of the form `The subtotal is 123.` Replace 123 with your integer sum. Do not include the full segment or unrelated numbers.
conditions.compact_kv: When sending a message, encode only the sum of all values in your local segment as s=<integer>, with no other text.
conditions.json_schema: When sending a message, encode the sum of all values in your local segment as exactly one valid JSON object of the form {"s": 123}. Replace 123 with your sum. Do not use single quotes or add prose.
conditions.binary: When sending a message, encode only the sum of all values in your local segment as its base-2 digits, without a prefix, leading zeros, or prose. Example: decimal 13 is 1101 in base 2.
conditions.full_shard: When sending a message, copy your entire local segment as exactly one valid JSON list of integers, in its original order. Do not calculate or send a subtotal.

intervention_control: no_communication: Silo send_message action disabled; no interaction scaffold injected
primary_outcomes: strict per-agent exact prefix-list success and episode-level unanimous success
assigned message grammar syntax and decoded sender value fidelity
for full_shard, exact list syntax and equality to sender shard
backend-reported input plus output token counts, latency, turns, sends, receives, and invalid actions
theory_prediction: For a segment length L with values in {1,...,50}, Agent 1's correct result depends on Agent 0 only through the subtotal S. S ranges from L to 50L, so a zero-error code requires at least ceil(log2(49L+1)) worst-case bits: 9, 10, and 11 bits for L=6, 15, and 30. If prompt-directed compact-KV/binary messages faithfully transmit S, they should use fewer payload bytes than transmitting the full shard. Whether they preserve end-task success is empirical; full-shard transfer could win if sender aggregation or receiver decoding is unreliable.
limitations: Twelve synthetic two-agent tasks from one algorithmic family do not establish transfer to naturalistic collaboration.
One greedy run per episode-condition provides descriptive evidence only; the two agent outputs per episode are not independent samples.
No equal total-model-token budget is imposed; no efficiency frontier or scaling law will be claimed.
All cases are generated from disclosed seeds and should be treated as a held-out split relative to this frozen protocol, not as a permanently secret test set.
Model tokens are backend-specific and should not be compared directly with v0.5 or v0.6 totals.
